title: Covid-era survival: automate your business by moving it online (Ross Jenkins, DigitalME)
summary: Ross Jenkins, founder of marketing agency DigitalME, argues that during Covid19 a business can either cut costs and wait or transform by automating. He uses a gym example (online sessions, a lead-magnet freebie, email list, pre-sold packages, membership site) and warns against DIY automation. Short and promotional, with one useful funnel pattern.

principles.text: In a shock, don't just cut costs and wait; push your boundaries and transform the business by automating it.
principles.quote: However, you could also push your boundaries and absolutely transform your business by automating it.

principles.text: Adapt the offer to the new reality: move in-person services online so the business keeps earning when the old model is blocked.
principles.quote: some gyms adapted by automating their services. They introduced group and one to one workout sessions online

principles.text: Use a strong free lead magnet promoted on social media to build an email list fast.
principles.quote: created an irresistible dream abs at home freebie, which they pushed all across social media. As a result, that helped them to build an email list fast.

principles.text: Monetize the list by pre-selling products, then package them into a membership site for recurring, passive income.
principles.quote: They used that email list to pre-sell meal plans and 30-day magic fat burn packages, which they then put into a membership site and now they’re making money in their sleep.

principles.text: Knowing how to automate isn't the same as making it work; the goal is a system that brings quality leads 24/7, so get expert help rather than DIYing CRM tools.
principles.quote: there’s a massive difference between knowing how to do something and making it work, so it brings you quality leads 24/7.
